reviews.text: I have been following the game for a few weeks because I loved Bloons but this game still needs a lot of work and has some issues that I find unacceptable for a 10€ game. However I also have fun with the freedom the game gives you and love the massive skilltree. Here is my feedback so far: + Love the pixel art style + Interesting new take on tower defense + Skill tree seems massive and challenge mode could allow for many hours of gameplay + Being able to move the hero is fun + Another promising indie game (I love indie games) - Game crashed after 14 minutes and I had to start all over (can I send something to you somewhere to fix the issue?) - The theme is kinda weird. Why do you have oranges as currency and have orange trees to defend? Why is the hero called Tangy like tangerines? There is also no story or anything that explains it - Only 2 achievements? And one of them has a weird placeholder title or description - The german translation is really bad, lots of typos, lots of English words left in instead of properly translating - Tutorial not skippable - There are only a few maps, I would expect more content for that price - I watched some of your streams and you seem to use the FreeType library. Yet there are no credits or anything I could have found that attributes FreeType according to the license. I don't know if there is also other stuff you used that you don't credit anywhere. Please respect peoples work and take the few seconds of time to give them credit! - There are no options for changing input stuff like keybinds or mouse sensitivity - There are also no accessibility options Please note that these points is all the feedback I can give right now, not all of these are reasons for my current negative review. I really hope you can improve the game further, I love the idea! I will happily give it another try and change my review!

Feels more like a tech tree grind game than a strategy game. Pacing forces you to replay earlier rounds a couple times to get the tech tree to a point where you can progress and yet it also very short. 8 levels. Feels very early access despite being complete.

This game is FAR from beyond saving, and it has a few nice features. But, the "real time" aspects, RNG, few options, and overall chaos prevent it from reaching the status of a good tower defense game. The tutorial is short (good!) but then throws you into a game where you have to read literally 3 paragraphs of text to understand a single item or ability, which are randomly generated in both the store and the battlefield. And, the best part, the game does not stop at all. There is no time to strategically place your towers, there is no time to read the thesis that will explain one of (maybe 100, I could not begin to guess) items that MAY generate in the store or chests (once again, only RNG here). These items can have unique functions, some can only be applied to certain "towers", and without applying them perfectly you will be unable to complete a mission. This is how the dev justifies their 3 total tower options, 5 missions (could be more later on, but not realistically different from the first one), and 1 hero that has to be manually controlled. There are hours of gameplay in this game because it is designed poorly enough that you have to repeat everything to get a 10% chance of success. The hero mechanic needs to be scrapped hard. Requiring me to right click 75 times in a minute window in a game I am just learning that you fraudulently call a "Tower Defense" to move one specific sprite around is garbage. Originally I denounce a review saying that this game only had 2 achievements (one that is literally broken). But now I see that putting any real measure on how many people are truly playing this game would only hurt it. Go ahead and look at the positive reviews and see how few mention the gameplay, the function, or the fun of this game. No one is actually trying to complete this slop. I am glad that most are at least trying to promote an indie developer, but we need to actually have some level of enjoyment to our games, or even indie titles are useless. Hoisting this game on top of some pedestal only hurts the industry even more. This dev may be able to make a good title, but they need 10,000 more hours in the kitchen and they need to consult some actual TD fans (as many of us as are left).

By stage 5 you're hitting a meta progression wall. The game clearly expects you to replay earlier stages and play endless mode to grind skill points. Tooltips also need work. They reference different mechanics but from what I can tell they're not explained in the game anywhere. For example, how does bleed work? How much damage does a burn do? What the hell is an intervene? Some of the tooltips reference unit abilities and cooldowns, but I was only aware of the healers ability, so i'm not sure what that does for the other units. I can certainly some guesses at these things, but the information should be there. Lastly, it's way too easy to accidently pull the boss on the maps where they sit on the map. Give your archer something that increases range, congrats the boss pulled. Accidently walk your hero too close to grab a chest, boss pulled. I think I also had one attempt where a projectile chained and pulled the boss.

UPDATE: can confirm.. any map is same - wave 1 - 5 easy, wave 6 is 5 times more difficult.. or 1-10 easy, wave11 is impossible. The balance in difficulty between waves is astronomical. The balance between world maps in difficulty is also not linear! Last update: well, dev does says "later more maps, more bosses, more items.." but... 8maps? i would expect game to have 30maps or similar.. will it reach that many? maybe it will reach 15maps eventually. overall: good game but its a minigame at this point. fun after you grind out. will change to recommended game once it has content. Now its not much, majority time spent on same few maps. Last map is cheesy and lame. :( EVEN THE SCREENSHOTS from game dev are straight up misleading. You see screenshots with 20-40 "towers". You cant have it, its only in endless mode. You cant get enough gold to even have 10-15 heores/towers before finishing the map which is ~10-12 waves. And endless mode is nothing, its just pointless chase for ego, its fun but optional. That means whole game you will play with only up to 10 heroes, which is also untrue, because to gear up each heroe/tower it costs, so you will end up clearing map with just 5 heroes.. ofc game is cool and has good skill tree but balance is based on who knows what. no other games has such spike difficulty, clearly rushed and not finished game. Its impossible to even say game is awful because im not sure how many maps exists! You cant know because you are stuck after mere few maps, slowly gaining skill tree points.

If like Tower Defense genre, this be another experience and add on in the list However, there's only 3 unit (as tower) for player to place on the map. Another is 'hero' in which player can control to help just a bit.. those unit can be upgraded on 4 different item slot to buff/give different attack style those unit can also be upgraded/buff with different talent, making them stronger in attacking enemy. The problem for me with this game, You will repeat playing same map over and over to get more talent point. Get used to this. Next is, no matter how level up your Hero is, every tower/unit is using the best possible loadout/equip with item that buff their attack.. the enemy will always win. Why is that..? Enemy will have their amount and HP (each of them) being buff for every round.. Unit/tower can only change equipment, that's it. Each unit/tower cannot level up like enemy do. Meaning sooner or later you will stuck having bunch of unit/tower being overwhelm by enemy unit. Always. You will not feel powerful at all in this game unlike any Tower Defense game. (At least that how I feel). The most problem for me with this game is.. ..the 'talent point', in which you can collect in the game by defeating enemy.. it is very limited. (it was 520 right now, before was 420 holy geez..) That's right. Once you collect enough 'talent point' allowed in this game.. ...You need to build your unit (tower) with specific build or talent wise due to limited 'talent point' to use. well.. is it fun for me then? (despite the problem I mention) the moment you realize the 'talent point' is limited (like I do) that's when you stop excited looking forward to play this game.. because you cannot upgrade everything.. on every unit.. in which there's only 3 of them in the game.. it's just not enough talent point given to player to feel really good and powerful (as it is right now) ,,and after think more on making this review, if you a Tower Defense maniac, enthusiast, try-hard, maso type of player that just excited in the face of challenge, by all mean this is one of the game you can definitely enjoy. No doubt. However as the time of me writing this review, of how I feel on this game at this moment... no. I cannot suggest this game to other people.. for now. Maybe someday in the future, (soon hopefully) if the talent point being add more, (at least 1000 skill point player can get/farm) or more new equipment to ease player enjoyment playing this game, (more of these, yes) maybe some enemy being nerf due to how unfair of their health and speed currently is.. (the boss is annoying) Maybe I revise this review back.. maybe. Cuz I forgetful see..

First off, solo dev actually made a game that works, they're updating things, they're active, this is all good. And I wanna be like "Awesome game, go buy it!" BUT. But I can't win. I just can't win. Levels are a slog; even putting points and gear into health, units get one shot; the bosses have devastating attacks that destroy any concept of strategy; the gear looks REALLY COOL and the abilities they grant seem awesome, but you can't buy gear when you have to buy 200 units - cause they all die instantly! The skill tree is also REALLY COOL and I want to love it, but the upgrades don't have any noticeable impact, and it just means that gameplay consists of playing the same stage over and over, losing over and over, trying to grind xp in the hopes that MAYBE your guys can live past one boss attack. I'm not gonna refund this. I WANT this game to be good. I WANT to support someone who is out there making games. I WANT to support someone who is actively working on making their game better. But... if you're thinking of buying... maybe wait a while and see if patches fix things up?

Is it worth 10 bucks? yes. Is it fun? yes. Does it have major balance issues? 1 billion yeses. I feel that this game has its heart in the right place, the idea is great! and from one small dev to another i love to support and try out things. This game is incredibly infuriating at times. The crafting system is the main issue i have i think. U can make items which is cool! You can combine similar things to get new things. U dont know what can and cant combine without owning combinable pieces. U cant see a list of items to compare items, so early in the game u are just tryn out pieces hoping they may or will combine. There arent many items, but so far it seems like half the levels out rn make it so cold/freeze items are useless. There are 5 statuses you can apply poison, bleed, ice, fire and lightning. Bleed and fire effectively do the same thing until you upgrade the individual towers' skill trees to make them do more. Even still, fire reigns supreme and its not even close. The pit level is annoying. You MUST play archers and ONLY archers in order to win. I feel like a level requiring ranged units is cool, bloons does it all the time, but that can work if there are more than 3 types of towers. The game also makes towers more expensive when you own more than 1 type of them, so it becomes harder to defend as time goes on simply because u cant play anything else. overall, i think it is a great game, or at least on its way to be one. I think there are some key design/balancing flaws that need adjusting.

Feels like the basis here is solid but the overall game just feels like a tutorial. Needs more levels, more challenges, and more reasons to use the other classes. I'm not a fan of the upgrades system either, as it feels tacked-on and ultimately pushed me further and further away from trying different strategies. Keep at it dev!

The game lacks foresight as a developer. I have 6 hours in the game. And im stuck on level 9? Like thats absurd. Not every level needs a gimmick. The game is wayyyyyy too grindy. I have 3 stars on all previous levels, I even have got to round 45 in challenge mode on a level. But I can't beat level 9? Alot of the skill tree upgrades suck, you really don't notice a change even after 10+ unlocks. Item randomness is too harsh, with how random it is, you really need like 8 item slots to buy from. Not getting a skill tree to improve the hero is also lame. Using the hero feels more like a chore then an actual benefit. Same with moving heroes. Again level 9 you just aren't allowed to move heroes... because...? Reasons? The game suffers from lack of foresight and balancing, and honestly you can't just sit down and beat some levels you have to... lose over and over or go back to some other level and play challenge to grind out skill points. Which just isn't fun. I feel like there could be a more fun gamemode to beat to grind skill points. But the face I feel like I need the archer skill tree maxed to beat level 9, is just idiotic. Maybe this level makes more sense later on in the game, but it feels like with each level you have to stop and grind a bit.

Like the warrior its nice using a singular one gives it the ability to hold back more but so many enemies can clump and void that or they just ignore defender naturally which also doesn't feel good on top of it all.

Although I enjoy TD games, I don't actually play many because I often find them either too easy or too repetitive. This one, however, has unique mechanics and is surprisingly very difficult. The movement system with Tangy is something I haven't seen before, and adds another layer to what might otherwise be a typical TD game. There are only three tower options + Tangy at the moment, but each tower has an extensive skill tree that lets you customize those towers further. Overall, I think it's very charming and I enjoy the sprite work and unique gameplay, but would caution anyone looking for a casual or easy experience. I actually really enjoyed replaying levels over and over trying to figure out my best strategy with limited currency and resources, but I can see how this would frustrate some players too.

I really want to love this game but it requires so much grinding basically incredible lengths for each boss to beat each them and you cant progress till you do( you will only be able to see the maps you already beaten which gets old fast) I really don't understand this system why a dev would do this, normally its fine if the game has randomly generated maps to keep it interesting. To give an example lets say a boss can only be damaged by fire and the only character that deals fire damage hits for like 40 damage right now unless I spend another ten hours of grinding then just maybe I can deal enough damage to beat it only the boss has million hp. the game seems to be only locked with three characters, if this game had a fourth hard hitting arty type time it would make much more enjoyable, the game over uses a revive system so it gives the characters nearly zero health making the system feel abused and only your hero that you can move around often gets one shotted you can put items on your team to prevent instant death but your hero doesn't seem to equip items to prevent that. What would help with the grind is either is to lower the boss hp a bit, or keep the current grind system and add lots of fun random side maps or random generated maps to keep the game interesting and add a fourth character a slow powerful damage type to deal some damage to the boss.

Very grindy but lots of fun! There are some really unique gameplay mechanics here that I like a lot. Also it's somewhat luck based but maybe that adds to its addictive nature. While you don't have too many types of "towers", you can individually upgrade them with various items, there is a lot of strategy involved here. I love that Tangy is actually a movable character who can level up during a run, also she can move others around. It has lots of depth. If you are OK with the grindy, kinda roguelike style nature of it, you will like it, but if you want something more straightforward, it might be a bit too much as it's a mixture of roguelite, tower defense, RPG, strategy with some luck based mechanics.

Ok, well, that was so fun for me that the i finished the game in 2-3 days (as you can see by the hours i played, yeah pretty fun one). Basically i was searching for some games from which you can relax and not have to worry about subscriptions or other annoying 'AAA' stuff that's apparently "normal" nowadays. First the MUSIC --> awesome, i was pretty invested in the game, gave me exactly what i needed and felt like the current map or circumstance should have Second the GRAPHICS --> it was continuous as it should be, nothing felt like it did not belong there Third the MECHANICS --> there is so much happening and you need to constantly check and recheck yourself and the position, and many stuff that you can actually do (there is also a non-serious type of competition with others, which adds extra flavour to the game) The rest --------> I was following the game comments on steam, people seem to be annoyed by the level of difficulty which i don't understand. Yes you need to use the brain (what doesn't require it btw?), but at the same time it does not feel overwhelming, it gives you space to think and iterate over your moves, and review your strategy before continuing. Knowing that the game was built from scratch by one person (not even using already built --game engines), without publishers or any kind of backup.. pretty much sums it all up. All recommendations !!!!

Unfortunately, I just cannot recommend this game. It is guilty of one of the worst sins a game can be guilty of: Wasting the player's time. What happens is usually this: You'll spend a very long time getting through a level to the boss. Then that boss will wreck you quite quickly (depending on the level). ---------- EDIT: It seems like some of what I describe below is due to 3x speed being broken, it appears that many shots just downright aren't counted as a hit and therefore won't damage targets, making especially bosses insanely hard it appears. Well, obviously that should be fixed. ---------- And so you grind, and you grind and you grind, getting more frustrated with each attempt as the game's mechanics are unfortunately somewhat obtuse. Once you understand (or look up) what the current boss's gimmick is supposed to be, you need to go back to the skill tree, and painstakingly respec everything to fit exactly that boss. What this game would absolutely need is a checkpoint before the boss and MUCH, MUCH, MUCH less gimmicky bosses that won't require the absurd respec dance every single time. As it is, you'll be endless frustrated by getting your time wasted. And that's not even the only issue: You are fully at the mercy of RNG. Didn't get the kind of items you need? Well, too bad, you're dead - or you'll waste precious gold to reroll until you get what you want. There is item conversion, but the cooldown is so long it might as well not exist. Needless to say, this only adds to the frustration.
